boundary: History index records are context objects for route activation and clustering. They are not automatic graph truth, permanent meanings, or standalone color claims.

lanes.label: Religion
lanes.description: Sacred structure, ritual systems, doctrine, worship, law, pilgrimage, reform, transmission, exile, and memory.

lanes.label: Arts
lanes.description: Image, form, performance, architecture, craft, symbolism, patronage, composition, medium, style, and visibility.

entries.label: Prehistoric religion
entries.summary: A broad orientation record for prehistoric sacred behavior, burial practice, symbolic objects, and ritual interpretation before written doctrine.
entries.sourceNote: Wikipedia orientation source for early ritual and symbolic burial context.
entries.boundary: Interpretive prehistoric evidence remains contested; use as orientation, not as final proof of one fixed belief system.

entries.label: Paleolithic religion
entries.summary: Orientation record for sacred inference from cave sites, figurines, burial, and repeated symbolic treatment during the Paleolithic.
entries.sourceNote: Wikipedia orientation source for prehistoric symbolic and burial patterns.
entries.boundary: Much of the record is inferred from archaeology rather than preserved written self-description.

entries.label: Art of ancient Egypt
entries.summary: An orientation record for funerary image systems, symbolic order, monumental form, and the relationship between art, kingship, and the sacred afterlife.
entries.sourceNote: Wikipedia orientation source for image, monument, and funerary symbolism.
entries.boundary: This record captures broad art-historical patterns, not the full range of Egyptian local practice.

entries.label: Ancient Egyptian religion
entries.summary: Orientation record for temple worship, divine kingship, funerary devotion, cosmic order, and sacred image use in ancient Egypt.
entries.sourceNote: Wikipedia orientation source for ancient Egyptian ritual and sacred structure.
entries.boundary: Use as a structured overview; practices shifted across dynasties and local cult centers.

entries.label: Art of Mesopotamia
entries.summary: Orientation record for relief, kingship display, temple image systems, and political-sacred monumentality in ancient Mesopotamia.
entries.sourceNote: Wikipedia orientation source for Mesopotamian visual culture and monumentality.
entries.boundary: This is a composite art-historical record across multiple Mesopotamian political periods.

entries.label: Ancient Mesopotamian religion
entries.summary: Orientation record for temple cults, divine-political order, sacred law, and ritual maintenance in ancient Mesopotamia.
entries.sourceNote: Wikipedia orientation source for temple-centered religion in Mesopotamia.
entries.boundary: Broad overview only; local cities and periods had different pantheons and ritual emphasis.

entries.label: Ancient Greek religion
entries.summary: Orientation record for civic cult, sacrifice, mythic transmission, oracle, festival, and sacred plurality in the Greek world.
entries.sourceNote: Wikipedia orientation source for civic ritual and mythic transmission in the classical Greek world.
entries.boundary: Not one centralized doctrine; practices varied by polis, sanctuary, and period.

entries.label: Classical art
entries.summary: Orientation record for proportion, body idealization, civic monument, order, and visible form in the classical world.
entries.sourceNote: Wikipedia orientation source for classical visual order and proportion.
entries.boundary: Broad art-historical label spanning multiple regions and centuries.

entries.label: Roman art
entries.summary: Orientation record for imperial display, architecture, portraiture, public memory, and civic monument in Roman visual culture.
entries.sourceNote: Wikipedia orientation source for Roman monumentality, portrait, and empire display.
entries.boundary: Orientation overview only; media and regional styles varied across the empire.

entries.label: Byzantine art
entries.summary: Orientation record for sacred image, iconography, gold field visibility, liturgical space, and devotional visual presence.
entries.sourceNote: Wikipedia orientation source for Byzantine sacred image systems.
entries.boundary: Use as orientation for iconographic and liturgical visual logic, not as a single universal meaning of gold or image.

entries.label: Christianity in the Middle Ages
entries.summary: Orientation record for church structure, monastic transmission, sacred law, pilgrimage, reform, and devotional institution in the medieval period.
entries.sourceNote: Wikipedia orientation source for medieval Christian institutions and devotional structure.
entries.boundary: Broad overview only; local rites, reforms, and political entanglements differed widely.

entries.label: Islamic art
entries.summary: Orientation record for geometry, calligraphy, ornament, architecture, sacred abstraction, and visual order across Islamic art traditions.
entries.sourceNote: Wikipedia orientation source for Islamic visual traditions and sacred abstraction.
entries.boundary: Islamic art spans many regions and periods; use it as an index lane, not a single style claim.

entries.label: Medieval art
entries.summary: Orientation record for manuscript illumination, liturgical objects, sacred architecture, iconography, and symbolic visibility in the medieval period.
entries.sourceNote: Wikipedia orientation source for medieval visual and devotional objects.
entries.boundary: Broad era label only; styles differ across geography, institution, and date.

entries.label: Renaissance art
entries.summary: Orientation record for perspective, patronage, body, visibility, classical revival, and the civic-sacred image in the Renaissance.
entries.sourceNote: Wikipedia orientation source for perspective, patronage, and image order in Renaissance art.
entries.boundary: Renaissance is a large label; this record should guide route seeds, not flatten all works into one meaning.

entries.label: Counter-Reformation
entries.summary: Orientation record for reform, doctrine defense, institution, sacred image policy, and devotional intensification in the Catholic response to Protestant change.
entries.sourceNote: Wikipedia orientation source for early modern religious reform and institution.
entries.boundary: Use as a reform-and-institution context object, not as an automatic meaning of any one image style.

entries.label: Baroque
entries.summary: Orientation record for movement, intensity, theater, sacred persuasion, ornament, and emotional visibility in Baroque art and architecture.
entries.sourceNote: Wikipedia orientation source for Baroque theatricality and movement.
entries.boundary: Baroque appears across secular and sacred settings; activation should depend on the current lane and route bundle.

entries.label: Modernism
entries.summary: Orientation record for rupture, experiment, abstraction, new medium, and the deliberate reworking of inherited visual language.
entries.sourceNote: Wikipedia orientation source for modern experimental form and rupture.
entries.boundary: Modernism is not one style; use as an index lane for experimentation and rupture.

entries.label: New religious movement
entries.summary: Orientation record for emergent belief communities, reform, innovation, charisma, and new sacred organization in modern settings.
entries.sourceNote: Wikipedia orientation source for emergent modern religious formations.
entries.boundary: This is a broad sociological and historical label; individual movements differ sharply.

entries.label: Pentecostalism
entries.summary: Orientation record for charismatic worship, testimony, movement, spiritual gifts, and intensified devotional experience.
entries.sourceNote: Wikipedia orientation source for charismatic Christian worship and revival structure.
entries.boundary: Use as a route-seed source for charisma, testimony, worship, and movement, not as a general statement about Christianity as a whole.

entries.label: Contemporary art
entries.summary: Orientation record for installation, concept, medium crossing, institutional critique, archive work, identity, and public context in contemporary art.
entries.sourceNote: Wikipedia orientation source for contemporary art structures and media behavior.
entries.boundary: Contemporary art is a broad container; route activation should depend on the specific work or context cluster.
